sources.entry: DevOps: Bringing development and operations together *(Atlassian)*

summary.title: What is DevOps?
summary.one_liner: DevOps is a culture plus set of practices and tools that merge development and IT operations into one continuous lifecycle, learned through its eight phases, practices, benefits, and adoption challenges.
takeaways: DevOps combines development and operations into a continuous, collaborative lifecycle, supported by automation and a shared culture.
The DevOps lifecycle has eight phases (Discover, Plan, Build, Test, Deploy, Operate, Observe, plus continuous feedback) shown as an infinity loop.
Core practices are continuous integration, continuous delivery, infrastructure as code, microservices, monitoring, and automation.
Main benefits cited are speed, collaboration, rapid deployment, quality and reliability, and security (DevSecOps).
Adoption is hardest on culture and team structure; start small with one value stream rather than an all-at-once transition.
summary.summary: This Atlassian article defines DevOps as a set of practices, tools, and cultural philosophy that automate and integrate software development and IT operations. It walks through the DevOps lifecycle phases, the role of toolchains (all-in-one versus open), and the benefits such as faster releases, collaboration, and security. It also covers adoption challenges, key practices like CI/CD, IaC, microservices and monitoring, and suggests starting with a small value stream. The page promotes Atlassian's Open DevOps solution, so some content is vendor-oriented.
